messages:
customer_jane: Hey team — we're seeing streaming completions drop for users behind our corporate HTTP proxy. Non-streaming (sync) calls succeed, but streams get reset after ~60s. Users report 'Connection reset by peer' and our client logs show a 502/504 from the proxy. Can someone help triage?

sam_support: Thanks @customer_jane — can you paste a minimal repro (curl + any proxy headers) and a tcpdump or proxy logs? Do you have the proxy vendor (BlueWall etc)?

customer_jane: Repro steps below. Proxy vendor is "CorpProxy v4.2". We see same behavior across different customer sites.

customer_jane: ```
# simplified repro (our client uses chunked streaming)
curl -v -x http://proxy.corp:8080 \
  -H "Proxy-Authorization: Basic REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams \
  -d '{"prompt":"stream test"}'
```

customer_jane: Tcpdump shows TLS packets flowing then RST from proxy after ~62s: ```
15:04:10 IP client > proxy: Flags [P.], seq 1:137, ack 1, win 229, length 136
15:05:12 IP proxy > client: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0, win 0, length 0
```

sam_support: Hmm. That timing smells like a conntrack/NAT idle timeout on the corp gateway. Streams tend to be long-lived but idle-ish from the NAT point of view. Does the proxy do deep packet inspection / TLS termination, or is it a straight CONNECT tunnel?

customer_jane: It's advertised as a CONNECT tunnel, but the customer says they have DPI enabled and sometimes they "peek" into TLS for policy. Vendor config is messy.

liam_infra: Quick checks: 1) confirm whether proxy is truly tunneling (shouldn't drop TLS RST normally) 2) check proxy idle timeouts and conntrack limits (many infra defaults kill flows ~60s). 3) try adding small keepalive pings or lower `TCP_USER_TIMEOUT`.

maria_devops: Also watch for header rewriting: some proxies strip `Proxy-Connection` and inject `Connection: close`, or replace `Content-Length`/`Transfer-Encoding`. If proxy rewrites responses it can turn streaming JSON into an HTML error (client then fails with parse errors). Can you capture the proxy's response body when it fails?

customer_jane: We captured the proxy return once — it was an HTML error page with a corporate block message, not a JSON error. So proxy is terminating/inspecting TLS in that case.

sam_support: That explains cert issues too — if proxy MITMs TLS you may get a cert signed by their CA and the client will error unless CA is trusted. For streaming specifically, DPI middleboxes often enforce a short DTLS/conntrack timeout.

liam_infra: Actionable repro suggestions: 1) run `tcpdump -w out.pcap host proxy.corp and port 443` on client side and share; 2) try the same request with `curl --http2 -v -x http://proxy:8080` to see if HTTP/2 keeps connections alive differently; 3) test from a box that bypasses the proxy (if possible).

maria_devops: Workaround ideas: - configure client to send tiny keepalive frames every 20s (e.g., send a 1-byte chunk or comment ping in the stream) - ask customer to increase proxy/conntrack idle timeout to >= 300s - disable DPI for api.redwood.com via proxy ACL (allow CONNECT passthrough)

customer_jane: Tried keepalive pings (1 byte every 25s) — improved but still occasional resets. Vendor says conntrack table also gets aggressively pruned under load. They're going to try raising the timeout and disabling DPI for our host in a test bucket.

sam_support: For our side: can you open a ticket with the customer and include packet capture and the exact timestamp (we want to correlate with our logs)? Also what client SDKs are affected?

customer_jane: Mostly Node and Python streaming SDKs. I'll attach captures and the SDK versions in the ticket. Ticket #SUP-8891 created.

liam_infra: One more note — if the proxy terminates TLS and re-issues certs, SNI could be rewritten/absent and backend routing might choose a different cert/virtual host. But since you saw HTML block pages, it's clearly terminating. If they can switch to true CONNECT passthrough, that should be stable.

maria_devops: If customer can't change proxy config, we can add guidance in our docs about keepalive strategies and a recommended minimal client config for hostile proxies (send periodic chunked pings, shorter application-level heartbeats, retry backoff). I can draft a doc once we confirm best practices.

ops_bot: [automated] Ticket SUP-8891 assigned to eng-infra on high priority.

sam_support: Thanks everyone — please post the packet captures in the ticket and any vendor logs. @liam_infra @maria_devops will loop in runtime team if we see anything on our edge causing early connection closure. :thumbsup:

customer_jane: Update — vendor raised conntrack timeout to 600s and disabled DPI for our host in test. Streams now stable over several hours. They'll roll to production next week. I'll update the ticket when rolled out. Thanks!
